newsitem.title: USA: Wis committee advances $37 bln fiscal 98-99 budget.
newsitem.headline: Wis committee advances $37 bln fiscal 98-99 budget.

text.p: Wisconsin's Joint Finance Committee has advanced a proposed $37.2 billion all-funds state budget for the fiscal biennium beginning July 1, a legislative aide said Tuesday.

The committee, which includes eight senators and eight representatives, completed its review of the state budget on Monday afternoon, said Robert Allen, an aide to committee co-chair Sen. Brian Burke, D-Milwaukee.

Committee members voted to use better-than-expected projected revenues to cover a $213 million pension fund settlement announced last week and also opted to raise the Wisconsin cigarette tax 16 cents to provide additional revenue for the state's general fund, Allen said.
The committee also advanced a $20 million income tax exemption for Wisconsin residents who earn less than $18,000 annually, Allen said.

Earlier in their review of the budget proposed by Gov. Tommy Thompson, committee members expanded the state's "healthy start" insurance program and advanced plans for a 1 cent-per-gallon gasoline tax increase and $5-per-plate motor vehicle registration increase.
The gasoline rax and registration fee hikes are projected to raise $153 million over the biennium as part of the $2.2 billion transportation pacakge, Allen said.

The committee recommendations included $440.8 million of bonds for construction projects, $12.1 million of general obligation bonds for the state drinking water loan program and $15.5 million of general obligation bonds for landfills, according to the legislative fiscal bureau.
The committee also recommended decreasing the bonding authority for the clean water fund by $8.4 million.
The budget plan has been forwarded to the Senate for consideration, Allen said. The non-partisan legislative fiscal bureau has scheduled a budget briefing for senators Thursday, he said.
Senators want to complete their debate on the budget plan next week and move it to the Assembly for consideration, Allen said.
